about.title: Chowchilla Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Chowchilla is a small city, but its roads carry a steady stream of traffic between Madera County farmland and SR-99. Public records show 17 injury collisions and 27 injured people in the most recent full year, with one traffic death — numbers that reflect real households dealing with medical bills and missed work. Corridors like Robertson Boulevard, W Robertson Boulevard, and Trinity Avenue see the heaviest reported volume, and crashes tend to cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., when commuters and weekend traffic overlap. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: photos, witness names, and medical records tend to disappear or fade fast. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured Chowchilla residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details and explain what comes next, free of charge.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Again

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Most car accident injury claims in California must be filed within two years, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a county road agency — is involved. An attorney can flag deadlines early so your claim isn't lost to a missed date.

items.title: Pure Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your fault percentage reduces the payout. Insurers know this and often try to shift blame onto you during a recorded statement — which is one more reason to talk to an attorney before speaking to the other side.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in car accident cases. An attorney working on contingency — no fee unless you recover — can help make sure those losses aren't undervalued or ignored.

items.question: I was in a crash near Robertson Boulevard and the other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: It's generally wise to hold off. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later, and anything you say can be taken out of context. An independent attorney can talk to the insurer on your behalf so you don't have to navigate that alone.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Chowchilla?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity — such as a county or city road department — may be responsible, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to get guidance quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame — your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. This makes it important to have someone evaluate the evidence carefully before insurers assign you more blame than is fair.
